newsitem.title: JAPAN: Pioneer suffers larger-than-expected interim loss.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer suffers larger-than-expected interim loss.

text.p: Japanese audio-visual equipment maker Pioneer Electronic Corp stayed deep in the red in the interim earnings period, battered by sluggish sales of its once mainstay product, laser discs.

But Pioneer, in the midst of a painful restructuring programme, remained optimistic about its business in the next six months, saying it has not changed its prediction of returning to the black in the latter half of the business year.

Pioneer said on Friday that its group net loss in the April to September period was a larger-than-anticipated 3.71 billion yen ($33.4 million), because of slowing sales of laser discs and other audio-video products.
It posted a group net loss of 4.26 billion yen ($38.3 million) in the same period a year ago.
A delay in the launch of digital video disc players in Japan -- a compact disc with massive recording capacity -- also hurt lift sales, a Pioneer spokesman said.
"We suffered slower sales at home, intensified competition and softening of product prices... The half-year results turned out to be very severe," said the company in a statement.
Group sales of its video equipment products, including laser discs, plunged 27.3 percent over the year-earlier period, the company said.

Pioneer took a special charge of about 12 billion yen ($108 million) during the six months to cover the cost of an early-retirement programme, in which it aims to cut its workforce by 650 out of 7,350 staff at the parent company.

For the full year to end-March 1997, Pioneer expects to halve its parent current loss to 6.6 billion yen ($59.4 million), from a 14.7 billion yen ($132 million) loss a year ago, after completing its restructuring programme.
Pioneer said it decided to forego both interim and annual dividend payments. ($1=111 yen)
